text.p: The winds of change blew again through the National Hockey League Tuesday as the Hartford Whalers became the Carolina Hurricanes.
The NHL team announced it would relocate to North Carolina in time for the 1997-98 season.

Whalers owner Peter Karmanos said the team will eventually play in a $120 million, 20,000-seat facility to be located adjacent to North Carolina State's Carter-Finley Stadium. Completion is scheduled in time for the 1999-2000 season.

The Eastern Conference club will play at the 21,500-seat Greensboro Coliseum for two seasons while waiting for the new arena to be built, said Karmonos. There is no word on what will happen to the American Hockey League's Carolina Monarchs, who play in Greensboro.

The Whalers become the third NHL team in as many seasons to relocate. The Quebec Nordiques became the Colorado Avalanche two seasons ago and the Winnipeg Jets moved to Arizona and became the Phoenix Coyotes last season.
Hartford had just three winning seasons in 18 years in the NHL and have failed to make the playoffs since 1992.

The Whalers were a charter member of the World Hockey Association, winning the league's first title in 1972-73. In 1979-80, four former WHA franchises were accepted into the NHL -- Hartford, the Edmonton Oilers, Quebec and Winnipeg. Edmonton is the only one of those WHA teams not to relocate.
The Whalers had demanded a new arena if they were to remain in Connecticut but could not agree on terms with Connecticut officials.

After talks with Connecticut Governor John Rowland, Karmanos agreed to make a $20.5 million default payment on the final year of the team's lease, allowing the club to leave Hartford after this past season.
Connecticut lawmakers, however, are balking at the agreement and are seeking increased compensation from the team.
